title: Ohio Is a Close Race Again This Election
summary:
For many years, Ohio has voted for Republicans in big presidential elections. But this year, the state is a battleground again. That means either party could win.

A group that studies elections, The Cook Political Report, says the races for Ohio governor and for a U.S. Senate seat are toss-ups. That means they are too close to call. Election Day is about two weeks away.

Many voters are worried about affordability, or paying for everyday things. In the city of Youngstown, many factory jobs left long ago. This summer, a bakery closed after 120 years.

In the Senate race, Democrat Sherrod Brown wants to win back a seat he lost two years ago. He says Republicans made life more expensive. His opponent, Jon Husted, says in an ad that 32 years in Washington is enough for Brown.

Gas prices went up because of the war with Iran. Husted said the war needs to end so prices can come down.
why_it_matters: The leaders voters choose can make decisions about prices and jobs that affect families like yours.
